result.topic_en: Euler computes the variation of ∫Z dx when Z depends on integral formulas Φ and Φ'. Introducing V=∫L dx and V'=∫L' dx, which vanish at x=a, he obtains the differential equation (N) − d(P)/dx + dd(Q)/dx² − ... = 0 for the extremal curve.
result.transcription:
124 DE METHODO
deinde vero est $\delta\Phi=\delta\int\mathfrak{Z}dx=\int\delta\mathfrak{Z}dx$ et $\delta\Phi'=\int\delta\mathfrak{Z}'dx$,
hincque propterea:
$\delta\mathfrak{Z}=\mathfrak{N}\delta y+\mathfrak{P}\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}\delta q+\mathfrak{R}\delta r$ etc.
$\delta\mathfrak{Z}'=\mathfrak{N}'\delta y+\mathfrak{P}'\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}'\delta q+\mathfrak{R}'\delta r$ etc.
ex quibus colligimus:
$\delta\Phi=\int dx(\mathfrak{N}\delta y+\mathfrak{P}\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}\delta q+\mathfrak{R}\delta r$ etc.$)$
$\delta\Phi'=\int dx(\mathfrak{N}'\delta y+\mathfrak{P}'\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}'\delta q+\mathfrak{R}'\delta r$ etc.$)$
Cum igitur sit variatio differentialis quaesita
$\delta\int Zdx=\int Ldx\delta\Phi+\int L'dx\delta\Phi'+\int Ndx\delta y+\int Pdx\delta p$ etc.
ponamus $\int Ldx=V$ et $\int L'dx=V'$, eritque vt supra,
$\int Ldx\delta\Phi=V\int dx(\mathfrak{N}\delta y+\mathfrak{P}\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}\delta q+\mathfrak{R}\delta r$ etc.$)$
$-\int Vdx(\mathfrak{N}\delta y+\mathfrak{P}\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}\delta q+\mathfrak{R}\delta r$ etc.$)$
$\int L'dxd\Phi=V'\int dx(\mathfrak{N}'\delta y+\mathfrak{P}'\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}'\delta q+\mathfrak{R}'\delta r$ etc.$)$
$-\int V'dx(\mathfrak{N}'\delta y+\mathfrak{P}'\delta p+\mathfrak{Q}'\delta q+\mathfrak{R}'\delta r$ etc.$)$
Ponamus autem, haec integralia $V=\int Ldx$ et $V'=\int L'dx$ ita capi, vt euanescant, posito $x=a$, ac praecedentium formularum partes priores sponte in nihilum abibunt, siquidem earum valores pro termino $x=a$ capi debent. Omnibus igitur partibus coniungendis obtinebimus
$\delta\int Zdx=\int dx\delta y(N-V\mathfrak{N}-V'\mathfrak{N}')$
$+\int dx\delta p(P-V\mathfrak{P}-V'\mathfrak{P}')$
$+\int dx\delta q(Q-V\mathfrak{Q}-V'\mathfrak{Q}')$
$+\int dx\delta r(R-V\mathfrak{R}-V'\mathfrak{R}')$
etc.
Cum

MAXIMORVM ET MINIMORVM. 125
Cum vero sit
$\int Pdx\delta p=P\delta y-\int\delta y\,dP$
$\int Qdx\delta q=Q\frac{d\delta y}{dx}-\frac{\delta y}{dx}dQ+\int\frac{\delta y}{dx}ddQ$
$\int Rdx\delta r=R\frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2}-\frac{d\delta y}{dx^2}dR+\frac{\delta y}{dx^2}ddR-\int\frac{\delta y}{dx^2}d^3R$
etc.
eliciemus variationem differentialem quaesitam
$\delta\int Zdx=\int dx\delta y\left((N-V\mathfrak{N}-V'\mathfrak{N}')-\frac{d(P-V\mathfrak{P}-V'\mathfrak{P}')}{dx}+\frac{dd(Q-V\mathfrak{Q}-V'\mathfrak{Q}')}{dx^2}-\text{etc.}\right)$
$+\delta y\left((P-V\mathfrak{P}-V'\mathfrak{P}')-\frac{d(Q-V\mathfrak{Q}-V'\mathfrak{Q}')}{dx}+\text{etc.}\right)$
$+\frac{d\delta y}{dx}\left((Q-V\mathfrak{Q}-V'\mathfrak{Q}')-\frac{d(R-V\mathfrak{R}-V'\mathfrak{R}')}{dx}+\text{etc.}\right)$
$+\frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2}\left((R-V\mathfrak{R}-V'\mathfrak{R}')-\text{etc.}\right)$ etc.
Coroll. 1.
Ponamus breuitatis gratia:
$N-V\mathfrak{N}-V'\mathfrak{N}'=(N)$; $P-V\mathfrak{P}-V'\mathfrak{P}'=(P)$;
$Q-V\mathfrak{Q}-V'\mathfrak{Q}'=(Q)$ etc.
ac relatio indefinita inter $x$ et $y$ exprimetur hac aequatione:
$(N)-\frac{d(P)}{dx}+\frac{dd(Q)}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3(R)}{dx^3}+\text{etc.}=0$
quae tamen iam inuoluit terminum praescriptum $x=a$, quia formulae integrales $V=\int Ldx$, et $V'=\int L'dx$, ita sunt captae, vt euanescant, posito $x=a$.
Coroll. 2.
Cum autem integratio huius aequationis, si fuerit differentialis, constantes arbitrarias inuoluat, si et hae determinationi nostrae relinquantur, vt formula
Q 3 $\int Zdx$

items.english: And the indefinite relation between x and y will be expressed by this equation: (N) − d(P)/dx + dd(Q)/dx² − d³(R)/dx³ + etc. = 0, which however already involves the prescribed endpoint x=a.
